items.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: I subscribe to Gerard Schwarz, do you know that name? He’s conductor of the Seattle Symphony.

ctx.x: What do you listen to these days yourself?

You know I got a nice set, I subscribe to Gerard Schwarz, do you know that name? He’s conductor of the Seattle Symphony. He was originally a trumpet player, like a virtuoso, and he became a conductor, it must have been like 20 years ago. I remember seeing him

at the Pasadena, the small chamber orchestra. And now in Seattle he puts out this thing of a two CD package of like the basic repertoire of symphony orchestras, and each set is a different composer. So one CD is the music, and the other CD is like a lecture, with excerpts from the music and explaining the form and a little bit of the history of the guy’s life and the period, and it’s very good. And like you’re just listening to — I’d had most of the stuff on LP, you know the music, but people say they don’t like…
